h2: Ultrasonic testing courses and certification for Boston-area technicians
html:
Ultrasonic testing courses and certification for Boston-area technicians

For ultrasonic testing training, the route in Massachusetts is the same as anywhere in the US: Level I and Level II under an employer's SNT-TC-1A written practice. Atlantis teaches UT theory as a self-paced online course with a practical examination, supports Boston employers through its Boston training page, and prepares candidates for the ASNT NDT Level III examination. Inspection scoping is covered further down.

Course or certification? The two are often searched as if they were the same thing. A course supplies the classroom hours. Certification follows only when the employer has also verified experience hours, vision and examination results against its written practice and signed the record. ASNT's own credentials are third-party certifications that sit alongside that employer system rather than replacing it, so a candidate should know which one a prospective employer expects before paying for anything.

The ultrasonic testing training course covers Level I and Level II theory, and NDT Level 2 training explains what changes when a technician moves from following instructions to setting up and evaluating. Boston employers putting a group through should start with NDT training in Boston or the statewide Massachusetts NDT training page. Practice on the Practical NDT UT simulator before the practical examination, add phased array training once conventional UT is solid, and use ASNT Level III preparation for Boston candidates when the time comes.

What a UT practical usually tests. Candidates calibrate on a reference block, scan specimens with planted reflectors, locate and size what they find, and write the result against the procedure supplied. Most failures come from distance-amplitude curve errors, missed scan coverage or a report that does not match the procedure, not from theory.

Massachusetts work that uses UT. The Board of Boiler Rules sets pressure equipment requirements in 522 CMR, and 522 CMR 15.00 adopts the 2021 National Board Inspection Code. Power boilers are inspected internally and externally at least once a year, with the external due within six months of the internal. A state District Engineering Inspector performs the initial inspection; later annual inspections may be done by that inspector or by an inservice inspector of an Authorized Inspection Agency, who must report to the Chief within 14 days.

  • Air tanks above 50 psi design pressure, six inches inside diameter and one cubic foot of volume are inspected at least every two years under 522 CMR 7.00, and UT thickness readings often give the inspector evidence on receivers that cannot be entered.
  • Inspected units carry a Massachusetts tag number, which belongs on every UT report so readings tie back to the state record.

Winter field work. New technicians in Boston learn quickly that cold changes UT practice. Water-based couplant freezes on outdoor steel, so glycerin or low-temperature gels are used; cables stiffen and batteries drain faster; and a probe moved from a warm vehicle to frozen pipe drifts until it settles. A good course covers why those effects shift readings; the practical examination and the first winter on site teach how to manage them.

Aerospace suppliers in the region often certify personnel to NAS 410 rather than SNT-TC-1A, so check the scheme before choosing a course. For inspection, see the national ultrasonic testing service and pressure vessel inspection in Boston. To arrange UT training for a Boston team, send a training enquiry.
